answer.sql:
WITH feb AS (
  SELECT location_id, COUNT(*) AS feb_orders
  FROM main.orders
  WHERE ordered_at >= '2025-02-01' AND ordered_at < '2025-03-01'
  GROUP BY location_id
), mar AS (
  SELECT location_id, COUNT(*) AS mar_orders
  FROM main.orders
  WHERE ordered_at >= '2025-03-01' AND ordered_at < '2025-04-01'
  GROUP BY location_id
), combined AS (
  SELECT coalesce(feb.location_id, mar.location_id) AS location_id,
         COALESCE(feb.feb_orders,0) AS feb_orders,
         COALESCE(mar.mar_orders,0) AS mar_orders,
         COALESCE(mar.mar_orders,0) - COALESCE(feb.feb_orders,0) AS diff
  FROM feb FULL OUTER JOIN mar USING (location_id)
)
SELECT c.location_id, l.location_name, c.feb_orders, c.mar_orders, c.diff
FROM combined c
LEFT JOIN main.locations l ON l.location_id = c.location_id
ORDER BY c.diff DESC
LIMIT 1;

SELECT c.location_id, l.location_name,
       COALESCE(feb_orders,0) AS feb_orders,
       COALESCE(mar_orders,0) AS mar_orders,
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(feb_orders,0)=0 THEN NULL ELSE mar_orders::DOUBLE / feb_orders END AS ratio,
       (COALESCE(mar_orders,0) - COALESCE(feb_orders,0)) AS diff
FROM combined c
LEFT JOIN main.locations l ON l.location_id = c.location_id
ORDER BY ratio DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

WITH feb AS (
  SELECT location_id, COUNT(*) AS feb_orders
  FROM main.orders
  WHERE ordered_at >= '2025-02-01' AND ordered_at < '2025-03-01'
  GROUP BY location_id
), mar AS (
  SELECT location_id, COUNT(*) AS mar_orders
  FROM main.orders
  WHERE ordered_at >= '2025-03-01' AND ordered_at < '2025-04-01'
  GROUP BY location_id
)
SELECT l.location_id, l.location_name,
       feb.feb_orders,
       mar.mar_orders,
       mar.mar_orders::DOUBLE / feb.feb_orders AS ratio,
       mar.mar_orders - feb.feb_orders AS diff
FROM feb
JOIN mar ON feb.location_id = mar.location_id
JOIN main.locations l ON l.location_id = feb.location_id
WHERE feb.feb_orders > 0 AND mar.mar_orders::DOUBLE / feb.feb_orders >= 1.5
ORDER BY ratio DESC
